HIST 210: American History 1865-Present

Instructor: Prof. James R. Fitzgerald

Semester: Fall 2026, begins September 1

Class Meeting: TR 11:00-12:30 PM, Humanities Building 405

Course Description

This survey course examines major themes and events in American history from Reconstruction through the present day. We will explore industrialization, immigration, wars, social movements, and cultural developments that have shaped modern America.

Course Objectives

  • Analyze primary and secondary sources critically
  • Understand multiple perspectives on historical events
  • Connect past events to contemporary issues
  • Develop strong historical writing and argumentation skills

Grading Components

Component Percentage
Participation and Discussion 20%
Short Essays (2) 30%
Midterm Exam 20%
Final Research Paper 30%

Weekly Schedule

Week 1-2: Reconstruction and Industrialization

Topics: Reconstruction policies, Civil Rights Act of 1875, rise of industrial economy

Assignment due Friday of Week 2: Reading reflections

Week 3: Immigration and Urban Growth

Topics: Immigration waves (1880s-1920s), urbanization, industrial working conditions

Essay 1 due Friday: "Immigration and Labor in Gilded Age America"

Week 4-5: Progressive Era and Reform

Topics: Theodore Roosevelt, conservation, trust-busting, women's suffrage movement

No major assignments this week

Week 6: America and World War I

Topics: U.S. neutrality policies, entry into WWI, home front mobilization

Midterm Exam due Thursday of Week 6

Week 7: The Roaring Twenties

Topics: Jazz Age, consumerism, Prohibition, cultural conflicts

Reading: Fitzgerald selections

Week 8: The Great Depression

Topics: Causes of economic collapse, Hoovervilles, social consequences

No midweek deadline; work on research papers

Week 9-10: New Deal and Franklin D. Roosevelt

Topics: WPA, Social Security, changing role of government

Essay 2 due Friday of Week 10: "Analyzing a New Deal Program"

Week 11: World War II

Topics: U.S. isolationism, Pearl Harbor, home front, Holocaust awareness, atomic bomb

Prepare for final paper research presentations

Week 12-13: Cold War Beginnings

Topics: Iron Curtain, Korean War, McCarthyism, nuclear anxiety

Research paper outline and bibliography due Friday of Week 12

Week 14: Civil Rights Era

Topics: Brown v. Board, Montgomery Bus Boycott, voting rights, Vietnam War opposition

No specific assignment date this week

Week 15: Modern America (1970s-Present)

Topics: Watergate, end of Cold War, 9/11, globalization, recent political polarization

Final research paper due Friday: "A Historical Analysis of [Your Topic]"
